page: Vultr vx1-m-4c-32g-240s is a memory-optimized server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a 240 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also perform in the top 25%, while Geekbench text processing reaches the top 10%. Multi-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores landing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth and database operations also perform at average levels, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Large LLM inference workloads show limitations, with medium-model prompt processing scoring in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server provides a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage further enhances its value for data-retrieval tasks. This hardware profile is well-suited for relational databases, caching layers like Redis, text processing applications, and general-purpose workloads requiring a larger memory footprint.
